en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-mahāsaptaratna-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
Translator unknown; currently appended to the Liang dynasty catalog.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Monastery. The Buddha addressed [the assembly]:
"Ānanda, you should receive and uphold this great seven-jeweled dhāraṇī mantra. Thereupon,
the World-Honored One immediately spoke it.
Syatāṃ dattam | Tiṣṭha loke | Prajñe | Pāra | Śikṣākūṭa | Pitānanda | If there be anyone who receives, maintains, recites, reads, and practices this dhāraṇī mantra.
Throughout their entire lives, they are able to cause all enemies and adversaries to rejoice.
Fire cannot burn them; blades cannot wound them; water cannot drown them.
They cannot be possessed by malevolent spirits or demons.
Whether it be devas, nāgas, asuras, gandharvas, or even humans and non-humans—
Ānanda, if this mantra of the seven jewels reaches them while they are amidst water or fire, or amidst enemies and bandits.
Whether one has consumed poison or encountered the effects of sorcery and spells,
one should recite this mantra;
then all fears, such as those that cause the hair to stand on end, shall be entirely liberated.
By means of the majestic virtue of Vipaśyin Buddha and the supernatural power of Śikhin,
compared with the wisdom of Viśvabhū and the precepts of Krakucchanda Buddha.
The merit of Kāśyapa and the diligence of Śākyamuni cause all sentient beings to completely eliminate their fears.
May you attain peace and well-being.
At that time, Ānanda, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
Thus concludes the *Sūtra on the Great Seven-Jeweled Dhāraṇī* spoken by the Buddha.
